study type: Case-control study (using human placental tissues) and in vitro experimental study (using trophoblast organoids and cell lines)
outcome: Expression and localization of p21, phospho-p21 (Thr-145), p27, p57 (protein and gene level)
Expression of fusion-related genes (syncytin-2, human chorionic gonadotropin)
cohort: Placental tissues were obtained from patients with early-onset preeclampsia (with or without HELLP syndrome), late-onset preeclampsia, and well-matched control women undergoing caesarean sections; also included were first trimester placentas and trophoblastic cell lines (BeWo).
finding: Cell cycle regulators are crucial for placental development, and p21 specifically influences multiple pathways relevant to the pathogenesis of preeclampsia, with its reduced level in fusing cytotrophoblasts in early-onset PE adversely affecting trophoblastic cell fusion.
mod_finding: Delivery mode significantly influenced placental gene expression, with CDKN1A (p21) and CDKN1B (p27) being notably upregulated in response to labor.
cross-section timing: At time of birth (for PE and control placentas) and during first trimester (for other placental samples).
gest_age: Early-onset preeclampsia, late-onset preeclampsia, and first trimester placentas were studied, but specific gestational ages in weeks were not mentioned.
